payload.rationale: The supplied Freddie Mac observations show the 30-year fixed mortgage average rising from 6.65% on August 20 to 6.95% on September 17, including a 19-basis-point increase in the latest week. With publication to two decimal places, YES requires September 24's first published value to be at least 7.02%, another 7 basis points higher. Recent upward movement makes that plausible, but five observations do not establish that the trend will persist. I assign a 45% probability, treating modest upward momentum as a judgmental assumption rather than an observed forecast. The strongest reason this estimate could be too high is that the latest unusually large increase could reverse or stall, leaving the weekly average below the threshold. The strongest reason it could be too low is that continuing increases in underlying bond yields or delayed lender repricing could carry the next average above 7.01%; the packet provides no direct evidence about those drivers. The estimate targets the first published September 24 PMMS value, not a daily lender quote or a subsequent revision.
limitations: Only five weekly observations are supplied; they do not support a reliable fitted transition or volatility model.
No contemporaneous Treasury yields, mortgage-backed security spreads, lender quotes, or observations for the September 17–23 measurement window are provided.
The probability is a judgmental estimate with substantial uncertainty about persistence versus reversal of the recent increase.
